changes_vs_current: Out (11): Led Zeppelin, Bob Dylan, Beyoncé, Pink Floyd, David Bowie, Aretha Franklin, Nirvana, Jimi Hendrix, Johnny Cash, Frank Sinatra, Bob Marley; In (11): Mariah Carey, Drake, Rihanna, Billy Joel, Eminem, Janet Jackson, Garth Brooks, Barbra Streisand, Chicago, Eagles, Rod Stewart; Michael Jackson falls from #2 to #7, Elton John rises to #2.
confidence: medium-low. Top 3 and the Beatles at #1 are solid (all four chart/sales lists agree; YouGov likability has them 4th, 12th and 13th). Things that look off for a typical American adult: Michael Jackson at #7 and Elvis at #4 behind Elton John and Taylor Swift; Beyoncé (average 33.0, lands just outside), Led Zeppelin (27.0) and Queen (#20) are low; Garth Brooks, Barbra Streisand, Chicago and Rod Stewart come from RIAA and Billboard longevity points, not name recognition. Spotify skews young and global (Bad Bunny, The Weeknd and Bieber outrank the Beatles there), and YouGov covers only 20 names and misses MJ, Taylor and Drake entirely. Positions 12-24 are bunched (19.8 to 26.6) and would reshuffle with another source. Nobody ran a national 'greatest artist' poll recently: the closest were Gallup 1999 (rock bands only) and Monmouth 2018 (Beatles 23%). A Family Feud 'biggest pop star' survey (Oct 2025) put Michael Jackson first, but only the article snippet was seen, so it is not used.
